title: Sports medical clearance
what: A doctor checks whether you or your child can do sports, and at what level. At the end, you get a clearance certificate.
why: Before joining a club, before competitions or fitness tests, or when a coach asks for it.
duration: usually 30 minutes to a few hours, if several doctors are needed; the certificate is often given the same day
tell_doctor: Chest pain, fainting, or shortness of breath during exercise
Sudden death at a young age or heart disease in relatives
What sport you plan to do, and how intensely

prepare.title: Checklist
prepare.text: Ask the clinic or coach which doctors and tests are needed for your sport.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No hard workout the day before. It can affect the ECG and blood pressure.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Comfortable sportswear and shoes, if there will be an exercise test.

bring: Vaccination record or your child's medical record
Club or federation requirements, if any
steps: The doctor asks about your health and training
Height, weight, blood pressure, and pulse are measured
Sometimes blood tests, an exercise test, or other doctors' checks
The doctor listens to your heart and lungs, and checks posture and joints
You get a clearance certificate, or are sent for more tests
feel: An exercise test is like a normal workout. You may get tired
after: Give the certificate to the coach or club
The certificate is valid for a limited time. Check how long
If something is found, the doctor will say what activity is OK for now
red_flags: Chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath during training: stop and call emergency services

faq.q: Why does a healthy child need an ECG?
faq.a: An ECG helps spot rare heart problems that are dangerous with intense exercise.
Usually once a year, sometimes more often for competitions. Check the club's requirements.

reminders.text: Sports medical tomorrow. No hard training today. Bring your documents.
